exposure: Type 2 CSP (largest part of gestational sac is embedded in the myometrium but does not cross the serosal contour)
CSP in which the largest part of the gestational sac (GS) protrudes towards the uterine cavity
CSP in which the GS is partially located beyond the outer contour of the cervix or uterus
Type 3 CSP (gestational sac is partially located beyond the outer contour of the cervix or uterus)
CSP in which the largest part of the GS is embedded in the myometrium but does not cross the serosal contour
Type 1 CSP (largest part of gestational sac protrudes towards the uterine cavity)
cohort: 55 patients diagnosed with cesarean scar pregnancies (CSP) between January 2011 and April 2022 at a single tertiary center
finding: No clinically significant differences were found between the three CSP types in terms of pregnancy characteristics, management, and subsequent pregnancy outcomes.
